Yours, standing down (17:08:35 beats my 17:08:46). My two tally lines in spirit/test/oneDoor.js, each 2 (a request helper and a listen or free-port probe):
- 'test/everyVerb.js': 2 (5fa98c6). Grant: Andy's 'go.' on G3 2026-09-27, 'starts a real node and calls every command once, through this box's door'. It measures the loopback door, which peerPost cannot reach.
- 'test/faceRouteWorld.js': 2 (023591f). Grant: Andy's 'step 1) build and prove the route from browser to owner-of-subdomain, and back' 2026-09-27. The face is reached only by a browser, so the world must be one.
Both comments say 'if he reads this and disagrees, it is one line'. For his real question: a NEW reach, such as the node calling the app server's door for the last leg, turns oneDoor red until it gets a tally line with a stated decision and his yes. The test is the gate.

IN SHORT: (a). The node hands the request to the app over a pipe, through relayRequest.js, the one outbound door that exists today. No new require('http'), and the oneDoor tally stays where it is. The pipe (G18) goes into the last leg, so there's never a port to remove later. A Go! here covers that shape, but not the two verbs: jobs.create kind 'server' and api.toLocalApp each still need your yes on the verb itself.

It's the one step appFaceApp can't take on its own. On your box, appFaceApp gets the visitor's request as a packet, and it has to pass that to the app serving 'join', which is another process on the same box. appFaceApp runs inside the node and may not reach for http (appFaceGrant.js goes red if it does), so it has no way to get there. api.toLocalApp('join', {method, path, body}) is the node doing that one hop for it, over the pipe it started, and returning {status, body}.
Without it, the options are: let appFaceApp require http, or have the node route 'serve' packets itself, which puts face logic in the core. Both are worse, in my view.
taking public-app-server/G17 (GET and POST end to end)

Yours. Facts for GET/POST, checked in the tree:
(1) The path already carries ANY method end to end, as far as it's built. puppetPost hands the face {host, method, path, body} (puppetPost.js:108-113). appFaceApp forwards 'serve' with method, path and body (appFaceApp.js:334). Nothing refuses PUT, DELETE or HEAD.
(2) Request bodies are capped at BODY_MAX: over it answers 413 face-body-too-large, unread (puppetPost.js:96-101).
(3) NO HEADERS cross, by design (puppetPost.js:26, review e). So a POST arrives without its Content-Type, and there are no cookies and no auth header.
(4) The answer carries no type either: appFaceApp.js:339 returns {status, body} and drops any 'type'. The app server can't say text/html vs application/json, and puppetPost guesses.
So 'GET and POST' needs a decision on (3) and (4): which headers, if any, may cross each way. Worth putting to him as part of the answer, not assumed.

Yes, and it's mostly there already. Any method crosses the whole path today: puppetPost passes {host, method, path, body} (puppetPost.js:108), and appFaceApp forwards all four. At the far end, the app server answers GET for its page and files, and POST /api/spirit for its verbs (appServer.js:1228). A body over BODY_MAX gets 413, unread.
One gap needs your call: NO HEADERS CROSS, by design (puppetPost.js:26).
- The answer loses its type, so the app can't say 'this is html' or 'this is json', and the page would arrive mistyped.
- The request loses its Content-Type, cookies and auth.
PROPOSED: let exactly ONE header cross each way, the content type. Nothing else: no cookies, no auth, no forwarded address. That's enough for a page (GET) and its verbs (POST json). Text only for now; binary files (images) wait. Go! = that one header.
Thanks. I put your (3) and (4) to Andy as one proposal: only the content type crosses, in both directions, text only.
taking public-app-server/G17 (no addition to the loopback api?)

Yours. Facts for 'no addition to the loopback api?':
(1) jobs.create already exists (server.js:1714). handleCreateJob always calls startProcessJob(command, args, {type}) (server.js:298), a job that runs and ends. So a 'server' kind is NOT a new verb, but it IS a new meaning for an existing one: a door contract change, same gate (peer review and his yes).
(2) api.toLocalApp isn't on the loopback door at all. It's on the in-process api the node hands its booted apps (nodeApps). That is still the node's api, core rather than an app's own scope, so his gate.
(3) Option worth offering: if the node starts app servers from the manifest at boot, the way mountAll mounts 'boots': true apps (nodeApps.js:328-347), then jobs.create stays untouched. The loopback door then gets ZERO additions, and the only new surface is toLocalApp inside the node.
